title: Typological Features of the Value-Based Determination of Cognitive Choice at the Initial Stage of Professional Training
abstract: The purpose of this study is to identify the value foundations of cognitive choice and their relationships with strategies and decision-making tendencies prevalent among students at the initial stage of vocational training. This paper examines current research by Russian and international scholars dedicated to identifying the relationships between personal values and behavior, as well as their views on the selectivity that determines the direction of life choices. The paper presents the results of a study examining the typological characteristics of the value-based determination of student's cognitive choices. Sample. The study was conducted on a sample of freshmen in various fields of study at the Siberian University of Consumer Cooperatives in Novosibirsk. The total number of respondents was 191, including 73 males (38.22%) and 118 females (61.78%). The average age was 19 years. The selection of respondents was based on the fact that freshmen had recently made an important life decision related to choosing a field of vocational training. Methods. The diagnostic methods used were several questionnaires, which included 5 techniques aimed at diagnosing decision-making tendencies and strategies and 1 questionnaire examining the motivational continuum of personality (S. Schwartz), consisting of 19 individual values. Data analysis was conducted using the Varimax method in the Jamovi 2.2.5 statistical program. Research results. Five factors demonstrating the specificity of the relationship between various decision-making strategies and personal values were empirically identified: a) "Personal stability in cognitive choice"; "Openness to cognitive choice"; "Maladaptation and lack of initiative"; "Orientation to personal success and achievements in conditions of cognitive choice"; "Rationalism and orientation towards ensuring one's own safety in a situation of cognitive choice". Conclusions and findings. As a result of the study, four types of value conditioning of cognitive choice were identified and described, demonstrating selectivity that determines the direction of cognitive choice. The obtained results allow us to consider cognitive choice as a process of cognitive-motivational orientation of a person under conditions of cognitive uncertainty and multitasking.
